transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, well, I guess I'm here because... I've been having a little trouble with eating lately. It's probably not a huge deal, but my parents were a bit worried, so I thought I should come in. Is that okay?

It's just that sometimes, when I start eating... it's like I sort of space out, I guess? It feels like I just disappear for a bit and something else takes over. And even in my head, I'm telling myself, you know, "You should probably stop now," but I just keep going until I'm so full I can't stand it. It sounds kind of silly when I say it out loud, doesn't it? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Can you recall what happens during those times when you feel like something else takes over while you're eating, or does it feel like you're not fully aware of what's happening at all?

Um, well, I guess I'm somewhat aware? It's not like I black out completely, it's just... I don't know, it's hard to explain. Like, sometimes after studying, I'll go to the dining hall and get a burger, and then I go back to my dorm room and... I just sort of keep eating. I'll have some cereal, and maybe some peanut butter, and just whatever snacks I have around. 

It's probably just normal college guy stuff, right? Just being really hungry after studying? But, um, I guess I do end up eating way more than a normal dinner. I just keep going until the trash can is full of wrappers and I feel completely sick to my stomach. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds really gross. Does that make sense, though? I hope I'm answering your question okay.
When you’re eating and you feel like something else takes over, do you feel like you can stop if you really try, or does it feel like you’ve lost control over your eating during those times?

Um, yeah... I guess that's the part that's a little embarrassing. It really does feel like I've completely lost control. Like I said, it's like I just disappear and something else takes over. 

Even while it's happening, I'm literally in my own head telling myself, "You really need to stop now, this is too much," but... I just can't. I just keep going and going until I literally can't stand it anymore. It's like my hands are just moving on their own. I know that probably sounds really weird, or like I just don't have any willpower or something. I'm trying to do better, I promise. Does that... does that answer what you were asking?
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to control your weight or get rid of the calories you consumed?

Um... well... I guess I do sometimes... try to fix it? Like, after I eat all that, I just get this overwhelming, terrifying feeling that all that food is just... sitting there, you know? Like it's instantly turning into weight. 

So, um... sometimes I'll find a quiet bathroom in the dorm, or maybe go to one of the empty floors in the library, and... I guess I make myself throw up. It's not every single time, I mean, I try not to! But it just feels like I have to get it out. I know it's really bad, and I shouldn't do it, and I'm really sorry if that's disappointing to hear. I'm not trying to be difficult or anything. Is it okay that I told you that?
Do you make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively specifically because you're worried about gaining weight or the shape of your body after these eating episodes?

Um, yeah... I guess that's a big part of it. I mean, I really don't want to sound vain or anything, I know guys aren't supposed to care that much about this stuff. But... yeah, I worry about it a lot. 

Like, I could be having a perfectly fine day, going to classes, feeling okay... but then if I just happen to catch my reflection in a dorm window or something, and I think my stomach or my face looks bigger than the other guys around me... it just ruins everything. It feels like I've completely failed, you know? Like I just want to hide and I don't want anyone to see me at all. 

So, um, yeah, getting rid of the food... it's because I'm so scared of looking like that. I'm sorry, I know it's a really stupid thing to get so worked up about. Does that make sense, though? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do these eating episodes or the behaviors you do afterward, like making yourself vomit, cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your schoolwork, relationships, or daily life?

Um, yeah, I guess it does... a little bit. I mean, I try really hard not to let it get in the way of things! I still go to my classes and everything. But... um... 

Well, I have kind of stopped going to meals or, like, hanging out with the guys from my dorm as much. I just... I get so worried they're going to notice how weird I act around food, or that they'll judge me. So it's just easier to stay in my room. And, um, my studying has gotten a little... messy, I guess? Sometimes whole nights just sort of slip away because I'm either planning around eating or... or dealing with everything afterward. 

I know I need to manage my time better, and I'm really trying to get back on track with my schoolwork. I don't want to be a bad student or anything. Is it... is it normal that it messes with my schedule like that? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
How often do these episodes where you feel like you lose control while eating happen? Are they happening regularly, like at least once a week, or less often than that?

Um... well... I guess they happen pretty often. I mean, I really wish they didn't! But... for most of this semester, it's been... um... several times a week, I think. Not just once in a while. 

I try to stop, I really do, but if I look back over the last few months, there hasn't really been a week where the whole cycle stopped completely. I know that sounds terrible, and I'm really sorry, I should have more willpower than that. I'm trying to do better, I promise. Is it okay that it's been happening that much? I hope you're not too disappointed in me.
Have these episodes of losing control while eating been happening at least once a week for several months now, and do they cause you a lot of emotional distress?

Um, yeah, I guess I kind of mentioned that just now... I'm sorry if I wasn't clear enough before! But yes, for most of this semester—so, like, the last few months—it's been happening several times a week. It hasn't really stopped for a full week at any point. 

And, um, yes, it does cause me a lot of distress. I hate feeling this way, and I hate that I can't just be normal about food like everyone else. It's really upsetting, but I'm trying really hard to stay positive and fix it! I don't want you to think I'm just giving up or letting it ruin everything. I hope that answers your question better? I'm really trying to give you the right information.
